practices_evaluation.justification: The test performs multiple distinct 'Act' operations: construction of Grafo and a separate null-string access causing a NullPointerException. This represents multiple behaviors in one test rather than a single Arrange-Act-Assert, so it is not atomic.
The test uses only local variables and does not reference or modify shared static/instance state. No @Before/@After required for this simple, self-contained test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class contains only one test method; while that single method includes an example of exception handling, there is not a clear pair of tests covering the happy path and a corresponding error scenario for the same behavior under test (e.g., Grafo). The requirement expects at least two tests per method under test.
The test constructs a Grafo and checks toString; there are no obvious numeric or range inputs or boundary conditions exercised in this method, so boundary-value analysis is not applicable here.
The test is short, self-contained, and does not duplicate setup across multiple methods. There are no helper methods needed for the single simple test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The method is short (< 20 lines), contains no loops or nested conditionals, and follows a linear Arrange-Act-Assert flow (aside from a small try/catch used to exercise a deterministic exception), so complexity is low.
The test contains multiple specific assertions (two assertNotNull calls with messages), which verify multiple properties rather than a single superficial assert, improving fault detection.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present. The tests appear active and runnable.
Class and method Javadoc include traceability information (REQ-001) linking the tests to a requirement, satisfying traceability practice.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit timing constraint; per decision rules the presence of a timeout indicates a performance-related check and thus satisfies this practice for this unit test.

The method name 'test0' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions (e.g., method_scenario_expected). Although Javadoc is present, the method name itself does not communicate the scenario or expected outcome.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: There are no clear signs of heavy auto-generated verbose code (the file contains a hand-maintained comment and focused tests). The absence of generation markers makes this practice not applicable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes Given-When-Then style comments in the Javadoc and inline comments, indicating BDD-style design intent and thoughtful test design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public APIs (constructor and toString) and does not access private internals or use reflection, focusing on observable behavior.
Assertions use specific methods (assertNotNull) and include descriptive failure messages, improving diagnosability of failures.
Comments and Javadoc succinctly describe the scenario (Given-When-Then). There is no excessive or commented-out code; comments add value rather than clutter.
The test contains no sources of non-determinism (no Random, current time usage, sleeps, or external dependencies). The included exception check is deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local variables and does not create files, persist data, modify static variables, or require cleanup; there are no side effects observable beyond the test itself.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: No @Tag, @Category, or equivalent annotations are present to classify the test. The class contains a single test but no categorization to enable selective execution.

practices_report.description: Each test case must focus on a single requirement or behavior.
Test cases should not depend on other tests or on execution order.

practices_report.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_report.description: Test cases must check both normal and edge case scenarios.
Tests should validate inputs at min, max, and just outside boundaries.
Tests should be self-contained and reusable; extract repeated setup into helpers.

practices_report.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_report.description: Keep test cases small and focused; avoid unnecessary complexity.
Assertions should be comprehensive and verify relevant properties.
Avoid @Ignore or commented-out tests; keep tests active and runnable.
Each test should be linked to a requirement via annotations or Javadoc.

practices_report.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_report.description: Performance and security must be tested separately and explicitly.
Test names should describe the scenario and expected outcome.

practices_report.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_report.description: Generated test code should be minimal and focused.

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_report.description: Prioritize tests and show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD-style).

practices_report.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_report.description: Tests should focus on observable behavior through public APIs.
Use clear, specific assertions with descriptive messages when appropriate.
Comments should explain 'why' and add value without cluttering code.
Avoid non-determinism (randomness, time-based, external dependencies) in tests.

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_report.description: Tests must not modify shared state or persist data without cleanup.

practices_report.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_report.description: Use labels or categories to organize and selectively run tests.
